decisions.decision: 'Remove' means fully delete the code (file + refs), not just disconnect it
decisions.rationale: Disconnect-and-leave is exactly how the dead-weight backlog accumulated; git is the safety net for recovery

decisions.decision: Cleanup is part of the commit process: change -> grep orphans -> delete -> build -> commit together
decisions.rationale: No dead code (or orphaned constant/local/comment) the change creates should ever land in a commit

decisions.decision: No automated pre-commit checks — DO NOT re-offer
decisions.rationale: User declined; a hook false-flags public API / cross-file use, so it can't replace the manual grep sweep

decisions.decision: Verify every removal with own eyes (grep all refs) before deleting
decisions.rationale: Audit labels are a starting point, not gospel. This session the audit had a wrong folder path (#21 was src/standalone not src/plugin), missed entanglement (#17 counter is incremented in the audio path + reset by a live fn; #21 orphaned the srcBits local), and a dac_noise header comment contradicted the code

decisions.decision: DSP math untouchable; CLI not cuttable; protective code never removed without asking
decisions.rationale: Bit-accuracy IS the sound; the CLI drives the golden corpus via regenerate_goldens.py / witness_diff.py

decisions.decision: Do NOT walk the user through invisible code internals
decisions.rationale: User is a recording/broadcast engineer, not a coder. Walking him through function-level cleanup in code jargon confused/frustrated him. Handle invisible tidying and report progress; only surface decisions that touch the sound or the interface, in plain language
